title: Media Release: Community Collaboration Leads to Stunt Driving Charge
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service would like to highlight the important role that community members of Chatham-Kent play in helping to keep our roads safe.
On June 3, 2026, a concerned citizen contacted the Chatham-Kent Police Service regarding a white pickup truck reportedly travelling at excessive speed on Pioneer Line between St. Clair Road and Prince Albert Road during the early morning hours. Acting on the information provided, members of the Traffic Management Office conducted targeted speed enforcement in the area.
On June 4, 2026, at approximately 06:50 hrs, officers observed a vehicle matching the description provided by the community member travelling eastbound at a significant rate of speed. Officers confirmed the vehicle was travelling at 175 km/h in an 80 km/h zone. A traffic stop was conducted and a 23-year-old male from Pain Court was charged with:
Drive-Motor-Vehicle – Perform Stunt – Speed in excess of 50 km/h, contrary to section 172(1) of the Highway Traffic Act (HTA)
Speeding, contrary to section 128 of the Highway Traffic Act (HTA)
As a result, the vehicle was impounded for 14 days, and the driver’s license was suspended for 30 days under provincial administrative penalties.
The Chatham-Kent Police Service encourages residents to continue reporting traffic concerns. When residents and police work together, we can address dangerous driving behaviour and help make our roads safer for everyone.

title: Media Release – CKPS Launches a Trespass Authority Agent Program for Business and Commercial Property Owners
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service is introducing the Trespass Authority Agent Program, a proactive initiative designed to help business and commercial property owners address ongoing trespassing and loitering.
The program allows registered business and commercial property owners to authorize the Chatham-Kent Police Service officers to act as their agent for the purpose of enforcing the Trespass to Property Act. This means that the Chatham-Kent Police Service may take enforcement action on behalf of the property owner without requiring the owner to be present at the time of an incident.
Property registration is important because under Ontario’s Trespass to Property Act, police cannot automatically act as an “agent” for every private property owner unless authority has been formally granted. A registration process creates a clear, documented relationship between the property owner and the police service, ensuring officers are acting lawfully and consistently when enforcing trespass issues. Registered properties will display Trespass to Property Act Agent signage identifying that police have pre-authorized authority to assist with trespass enforcement.
The program is designed to support property owners in maintaining a safe and secure environment. The Trespass Authority Agent Program applies to properties specifically enrolled in the program.
Business and commercial property owners are encouraged to register directly using the following link:
https://www.services.tryrubicon.com/chatham-kent-police-service/registries/select
The Chatham-Kent Police Service remains committed to working with property owners and community partners to enhance safety and security.

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service Supports Canada Road Safety Week 2026
content:

“Our goal is simple, to help prevent collisions, injuries and fatalities on our roads. Every safe decision made behind the wheel can make a difference,” said Acting Sergeant Lisa Rodger.

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service responds to Fatal Train Incident
content:
On May 10, 2026, at approximately 14:08 hrs, Chatham-Kent Police Service responded to a report of a pedestrian struck by an eastbound passenger train in Chatham-Kent. The incident occurred on railway tracks in the area of Northwood Line. Despite emergency measures taken by the train operator, the individual, a 34-year-old male from Chatham, sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced deceased at the scene.
Officers secured the scene and the Traffic Management Unit was called in to investigate and coordinate with railway police and the Office of the Chief Coroner as part of the investigation. The rail corridor was temporarily closed while investigators conducted their work, and the train was later permitted to continue.
There is no ongoing risk to public safety. Out of respect for the family, no further details will be released.
Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones affected by this incident. On behalf of all members, we extend our deepest condolences during this incredibly difficult time, and we ask that the community respect the family’s privacy as they grieve.
If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available 24/7. In Canada, call or text 9-8-8 for immediate, confidential support. In an emergency, call 9-1-1. Those with additional information surrounding this incident can contact the investigating officer Cst. Joel Rehill, at 519-355-1092 or by email at joelr@chatham-kent.ca

title: Media Release: Single-Vehicle Collision on Erie Street South Leaves Driver with Life-Threatening Injuries
content:
On June 12, 2026, at approximately 16:29 hrs., Chatham-Kent Police Service responded to a report of a motor vehicle collision on Erie Street South, Romney Township.
The investigation revealed that a single motor vehicle, operated by a 57-year-old male from Wheatley, struck a berm before becoming airborne and landing on the beach. No other vehicles or individuals were involved in the collision.
The driver sustained life-threatening injuries and was transported to the hospital for medical treatment. He was initially taken to Leamington District Memorial Hospital before being transferred to Windsor Regional Hospital.
Due to the severity of the collision and the injuries sustained, members of the Traffic Management Unit attended the scene and assumed responsibility for the investigation. Erie Street South was closed for several hours but has since been reopened.

title: Media Release – Serious Collision Sends Two Individuals to Hospital with Life-Threatening Injuries
content:
On June 27, 2026, at approximately 22:11 hrs., the Chatham-Kent Police Service responded to a report of a serious motor vehicle collision at the intersection of Richmond Street and Inshes Avenue
,
Chatham.
The collision involved a single motor vehicle operated by a 38-year-old male from Chatham
,
with one passenger
,
and a motorized scooter with two occupants
:
a 41-year-old male and a 28-year-old male, both from Chatham.
The investigation
determined
that the motor vehicle was travelling eastbound on Richmond Street when the motorized scooter, travelling northbound, entered the intersection. Both occupants of the motorized scooter were seriously injured and transported to Chatham-Kent Health Alliance, Public General Hospital, before being transferred to Windsor Regional Hospital with life-threatening injuries. The occupants of the motor vehicle were both uninjured.
Due to the severity of the collision, members of the Chatham-Kent Police Service Traffic Management Unit assumed responsibility for the investigation.
The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has information that may assist investigators is encouraged to contact the investigating officer, Constable Joel Rehill, at 519-355-1092 or by email at joelr@chatham-kent.ca. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Media Release – Arrest Made Following Home Invasion, Firearm Incident and Drug Trafficking Investigation
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service has arrested one individual following an investigation into a home invasion, firearms offences and drug trafficking that occurred on the evening of July 11, 2026.
At approximately 21:00 hrs., police responded to reports of a home invasion at a residence on Taylor Avenue in Chatham. Two suspects gained entry into the residence and demanded property from the occupant before fleeing the scene. The incident escalated into a disturbance involving multiple individuals in the surrounding area when a witness observed a male suspect discard suspected controlled substances while attempting to leave the area. Concerned for public safety, the witness intervened and restrained the suspect until police arrived. While being restrained, the suspect allegedly produced a handgun
,
which discharged during the struggle. The witness was able to gain control of the firearm and maintain custody of the suspect until officers arrived and took him into custody. No injuries were reported in relation to the incident.
As a result of the investigation, a 25-year-old London resident has been charged with numerous Criminal Code and Controlled Drugs and Substances Act offences, including:
Robbery with a firearm
Disguise with intent
Possession of cocaine for the purpose of trafficking
Possession of methamphetamine for the purpose of trafficking
Assault with a weapon
Discharging a firearm in a reckless manner
Unauthorized possession of a firearm
Possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose
Careless carrying of a firearm
Obstructing a peace officer
The accused remains in custody pending a bail hearing. As the investigation progressed, members of the Chatham-Kent Police Service Intelligence Unit obtained and executed a Controlled Drugs and Substances Act search warrant at a residence connected to the investigation. During the search, officers seized drug trafficking paraphernalia, including digital scales, packaging materials and a debt list. Investigators also seized 43 grams of cocaine
,
31.5 grams of methamphetamine and a quantity of prescription medication with an estimated value of
$6,000
.
The investigation remains ongoing. Police continue to review surveillance footage and other evidence in an effort to identify the additional suspect believed to be involved in the home invasion. Further charges are anticipated as the investigation continues.
The incident appears to be isolated
;
the occupant of the residence was not harmed and there is no ongoing risk to public safety.
The Chatham-Kent Police Service is also reminding members of the public to exercise caution when witnessing criminal activity. While we recognize and appreciate the desire of community members to assist, situations involving suspected offenders can escalate rapidly and unpredictably, particularly when weapons may be involved.
Members of the public are encouraged to be good witnesses rather than placing themselves at risk. If you observe a crime in progress, contact police immediately, maintain a safe distance, and provide responding officers with as much information as possible, including descriptions of individuals, vehicles and direction of travel. Personal safety should always remain the priority, as attempting to physically intervene can result in serious injury or death.
Anyone with information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the Chatham-Kent Police Service at (519) 352-1234 or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Media Release – Arson Investigation Results in Charges Against Chatham Woman
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service has arrested a 35-year-old Chatham woman in connection with a suspicious fire that occurred on July 14, 2026, at a vacant residence on Park Street. At approximately 6:33 hrs., on July 14, 2026, emergency services responded to multiple reports of a structure fire at a residence in the 100 block of Park Street in Chatham. Chatham-Kent Police Service officers attended alongside Chatham-Kent Fire Department personnel and Chatham-Kent EMS.
The fire originated at the rear of a vacant residence and quickly spread to two neighbouring properties. One of the neighbouring homes was occupied at the time by four residents who were asleep when the fire spread to their residence. All occupants were able to safely evacuate without injury.
As part of the investigation, officers obtained and reviewed surveillance video. The footage captured a female observed on the property prior to the fire, including in the area where the fire is believed to have originated. Additional video evidence showed the same individual on the property earlier that morning.
The investigation was conducted in partnership with the Ontario Fire Marshal’s Office. Investigators determined that the fire was intentionally set.
Through the review of surveillance footage, witness statements, and additional investigative steps, police identified a suspect. Investigators further linked the suspect to clothing and personal property observed in video footage recorded on multiple occasions.
On July 16, 2026, members of the Chatham-Kent Police Service located and arrested a 35-year-old Chatham woman. At the time of her arrest, officers recovered several items believed to be relevant to the investigation.
The accused has been charged with:
Arson – Damage to Property
Arson – Disregard for Human Life
The accused was held for bail proceedings
The Chatham-Kent Police Service would like to acknowledge the assistance of community members who provided video surveillance and information that contributed significantly to the investigation, as well as the support and expertise provided by the Ontario Fire Marshal’s Office.
Anyone with additional information related to this incident is encouraged to contact the Chatham-Kent Police Service at 519-352-1234. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service and St. Clair Catholic District School Board Celebrate Partnership in Supporting Public Safety Training
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service (CKPS) and the St. Clair Catholic District School Board (SCCDSB) are proud to recognize a successful partnership that will strengthen emergency preparedness and enhance public safety across the region.
Through this collaboration, the St. Clair Catholic District School Board has provided access to local school facilities, enabling the Chatham-Kent Police Service to deliver Immediate Rapid Deployment (IRD) training to all frontline officers while also supporting training for officers from several neighbouring police services.
Immediate Rapid Deployment (IRD) training prepares officers to respond effectively to critical incidents in schools and the community. To meet provincial policing standards, officers must train in environments that closely replicate real-world settings. The use of school facilities has allowed the Chatham-Kent Police Service to provide realistic, high-quality training while maintaining compliance with current provincial training requirements.
Training will take place throughout the week of
July 27 to July 31, 2026, between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., at George P. Vanier Catholic School in Chatham.
Members of the public may notice an increased police presence in the area during these times. The training will occur only while the school is unoccupied and there is no risk to the public. This training is part of routinely scheduled, provincially mandated police training and is not in response to any specific threat or incident.
“This continued and valuable partnership between St. Clair Catholic and Chatham-Kent Police is important because it helps ensure the safety and well-being of both our schools and community. We are happy to assist our local law enforcement in any way possible because when we work together, everyone benefits,” said Lisa Demers, CEO and CEdO of St. Clair Catholic District School Board.
The Chatham-Kent Police Service extends its sincere appreciation to the St. Clair Catholic District School Board for its ongoing support and commitment to community safety. By working together, both organizations continue to demonstrate the value of strong community partnerships and a shared commitment to creating safer schools and stronger communities.

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service Investigating Fatal Two-Vehicle Collision
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service Traffic Management Unit is investigating a fatal two-vehicle collision that occurred on Queen’s Line in the early morning hours of Sunday, July 26, 2026. At approximately 12:06 a.m., emergency services responded to a two-vehicle collision on Queen’s Line between Bloomfield Road and Dillon Road.
The vehicles were operated by a 46-year-old male from Tilbury and a 57-year-old male from Chatham, who were the sole occupants of their respective vehicles. Both drivers sustained injuries and were transported to Chatham-Kent Health Alliance’s Public General Hospital for treatment.
Due to the severity of his injuries, the 57-year-old male was subsequently airlifted to London Health Sciences Centre, where he later succumbed to his injuries. The Chatham-Kent Police Service extends its sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of the deceased during this difficult time.
Given the severity of the collision, members of the Traffic Management Unit attended the scene to conduct a detailed investigation and reconstruction of the collision. As a result, Queen’s Line remained closed for several hours overnight and reopened early in the morning.
The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has information regarding the circumstances leading up to it is encouraged to contact Constable Shelton Richardson of the Traffic Management Unit at 519-355-1092 or by email at
sheltonr@chatham-kent.ca
. Information can also be provided anonymously through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service Reports Significant Decrease in Crime Severity Index in 2025
content:
CHATHAM-KENT, ON – The Chatham-Kent Police Service (CKPS) is pleased to report a significant decline in the community’s Crime Severity Index (CSI) in 2025, reflecting continued progress in public safety through proactive policing, strategic enforcement and strong community partnerships.
Statistics Canada’s Crime Severity Index measures both the volume and seriousness of police-reported crime. Compared to 2024, Chatham-Kent recorded decreases across all three CSI categories:
These positive results reflect the ongoing dedication and professionalism of CKPS sworn and civilian members, as well as the support of community partners and residents who continue to work alongside police to enhance public safety.
The reduction in crime is the result of focused enforcement initiatives, intelligence-led policing, targeted efforts to address repeat and high-risk offenders, investments in technology and training, proactive crime prevention strategies and collaborative partnerships with municipal departments, health-care providers, social service agencies and community organizations.
CKPS also recognizes and values the continued support of the Chatham-Kent community.
Public safety is a shared responsibility and the Service appreciates the collaboration of residents, businesses and partner agencies who contribute to making Chatham-Kent a safer place to live, work and raise a family. Continued investments in policing, technology, training, and staffing help ensure members have the resources necessary to respond effectively to emerging challenges and provide the level of service the community expects and deserves.
While the decrease in crime is encouraging, CKPS recognizes there is still work to be done. The Service remains committed to reducing violent crime, addressing repeat offenders, supporting victims and working closely with community partners to address the root causes of crime, victimization and social disorder.
“These results demonstrate the dedication and professionalism of our sworn and civilian members, as well as the strength of the partnerships we have built throughout Chatham-Kent,” said Chief Kirk Earley. “A nearly 12 per cent reduction in our overall Crime Severity Index is a significant achievement and reflects our commitment to proactive policing, community engagement and focused enforcement. We are grateful for the continued support of our community. While these results are encouraging, statistics tell only part of the story. Understanding community perceptions of safety remains equally important, and we remain committed to addressing concerns and enhancing public safety for everyone who calls Chatham-Kent home.”
The Chatham-Kent Police Service will continue building on this momentum through intelligence-led policing, strategic enforcement, crime prevention initiatives, community engagement and sustained collaboration with local partners. Together, these efforts will help create an even safer Chatham-Kent for residents, businesses and visitors.

title: Media Release – Search Warrant Execution Results in Multiple Drug and Weapons Charges
content:
The Chatham-Kent Police Service has charged nine individuals following the execution of a search warrant in Wallaceburg.
On July 29, 2026, members of the Chatham-Kent Police Service Intelligence Unit, assisted by the Emergency Response Team, executed a search warrant at a residence on King Street in Wallaceburg as part of an ongoing fentanyl trafficking investigation. During the execution of the warrant, officers located and arrested nine individuals inside the residence. A systematic search of the property resulted in the seizure of:
Approximately 51 grams of fentanyl
Approximately 27 grams of methamphetamine
Nine oxycodone tablets
Digital scales
Drug packaging materials
Canadian currency
Cellular telephones
Seven BB guns
A firearm receiver
Three compound bows
Brass knuckles
Various types of ammunition
The estimated street value of the controlled substances seized is approximately $11,900.
As a result of the investigation, nine individuals from Wallaceburg were arrested:
A 45-year-old male has been charged with:

title: Media Release – Chatham-Kent Police Service is Investigating a serious collision on Communication Road
content:
On August 13, 2026, at approximately 20:13 hrs, Chatham Kent Police Service responded to a report of a motor vehicle collision on Communication Road between Drury Line and Burk Line, in the Municipality of Chatham-Kent.
The investigation revealed that a single motor vehicle, operated by a 33-year-old male from Chatham, lost control before leaving the roadway.
There were two other occupants in the vehicle, a 25-year-old male from Blenheim and a 16-year-old female from Chatham. Both passengers sustained injuries, with one suffering life-threatening injuries. The passengers were transported to Chatham-Kent Health Alliance for medical treatment. The 16-year-old passenger was later transported to Victoria Hospital in London for further medical care.
Due to the severity of the collision and the injuries sustained, members of the Traffic Management Unit attended the scene and assumed responsibility for the investigation. Communication Road was closed for several hours but has since been reopened.
The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has information that may assist investigators is encouraged to contact Constable Shelton Richardson at 519-355-1092 or by email at
sheltonr@chatham-kent.ca
. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).
